cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Class barriers – The core thematic concept of class barriers as explored and highlighted in 'The Iron Lady'.

p.em: Example: The narrative of 'The Iron Lady' brilliantly scrutinizes class barriers to build character depth as Margaret Thatcher confronts confronting class barriers, parliamentary debates, and late-life cognitive decline.

cosy-blockquote.p: parliamentary speech – The core thematic concept of parliamentary speech as explored and highlighted in 'The Iron Lady'.

p.em: Example: The narrative of 'The Iron Lady' brilliantly scrutinizes parliamentary speech to build character depth as Margaret Thatcher confronts confronting class barriers, parliamentary debates, and late-life cognitive decline.

cosy-blockquote.p: cognitive decay – The core thematic concept of cognitive decay as explored and highlighted in 'The Iron Lady'.

p.em: Example: The narrative of 'The Iron Lady' brilliantly scrutinizes cognitive decay to build character depth as Margaret Thatcher confronts confronting class barriers, parliamentary debates, and late-life cognitive decline.

cosy-blockquote.p: Paranoia – The core thematic concept of paranoia as explored and highlighted in 'The Iron Lady'.

p.em: Example: The narrative of 'The Iron Lady' brilliantly scrutinizes paranoia to build character depth as Margaret Thatcher confronts confronting class barriers, parliamentary debates, and late-life cognitive decline.

cosy-blockquote.p: Guilt-stricken – The core thematic concept of guilt-stricken as explored and highlighted in 'The Iron Lady'.

p.em: Example: The narrative of 'The Iron Lady' brilliantly scrutinizes guilt-stricken to build character depth as Margaret Thatcher confronts confronting class barriers, parliamentary debates, and late-life cognitive decline.

cosy-blockquote.p: Compromise – (noun/verb) an agreement reached by mutual concession.

p.em: Example: The couple struggles to find a fair compromise between career and family.

cosy-blockquote.p: parliament – (noun/expression) a key word or expression featured in the film.

p.em: Example: Characters in the movie naturally use 'parliament' in conversation to highlight key emotional context.

cosy-blockquote.p: prime minister – (noun/expression) a key word or expression featured in the film.

p.em: Example: Characters in the movie naturally use 'prime minister' in conversation to highlight key emotional context.

cosy-blockquote.p: strike – (noun/expression) a key word or expression featured in the film.

p.em: Example: Characters in the movie naturally use 'strike' in conversation to highlight key emotional context.

cosy-blockquote.p: Narrative Clue – (noun/expression) a key word or expression featured in the film.

p.em: Example: Characters in the movie naturally use 'Narrative Clue' in conversation to highlight key emotional context.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Deconstruct the visceral opening sequence of 'The Iron Lady'. How does the visual establishment of class barriers within the House of Commons in London initiate the dramatic tension? Use formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ If you had to navigate the intense psychological parameters of the House of Commons in London, how would you safeguard your values against class barriers?

How does the director strategically introduce the motif of parliamentary speech early on to prepare the audience for the upcoming conflict? Deploy formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ Have you ever experienced a paradigm shift where your own understanding of parliamentary speech was radically challenged?

Analyze the psychological disintegration of Margaret Thatcher as their obsession with cognitive decay alienates her husband Denis Thatcher, parliamentary ministers, and critics. Formulate your thesis using formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ Does the cinematic representation of cognitive decay align with the socio-psychological realities you observe today?

In what ways do the quiet, domestic intervals in the House of Commons in London heighten the subtextual friction of paranoia? Discuss using formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ How do you personally maintain equilibrium when caught in an ideological conflict concerning paranoia?

To what degree does Margaret Thatcher's defense mechanism regarding guilt-stricken shield them from accepting their ultimate fate? Use formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ If you were called upon to intervene in Margaret Thatcher's descent into guilt-stricken, what cognitive intervention would you suggest?

The screenplay deploys the nuanced colloquialism 'compromise' to mask a dark secret in the House of Commons in London. How does this choice build suspense? Focus on formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ Do you find that acquiring highly idiomatic registers like 'compromise' enhances your linguistic empathy, or do you prefer formal competence?

How does the organic integration of the phrase 'parliament' during a crucial confrontation illuminate the power dynamics? Use formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ Have you ever integrated a highly localized idiom like 'parliament' into your conversational repertoire? Detail the outcome.

Deconstruct the linguistic subtext of the scene where 'prime minister' is used to convey a hidden motive during confronting class barriers, parliamentary debates, and late-life cognitive decline. Use formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ What conceptual challenges arise when attempting to translate a specialized expression like 'prime minister' into your native tongue?

How does the climactic revelation of 'strike' fundamentally reframe the narrative trajectory and alter our perception? Use formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ In high-stakes communications, do you tend to resort to indirect colloquial markers like 'strike' to soften your delivery?

If Margaret Thatcher had surrendered their denial of 'narrative clue' earlier, how would the screenplay's resolution have changed? Speculate with formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ What does your favorite piece of dialogue from 'The Iron Lady' reveal about your own aesthetic preferences in dramatic writing?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
'Margaret Thatcher's story of class barriers in 'The Iron Lady' is very sad, and they should be more careful.' Do you agree? Use formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ If you were a film maker, would you make a movie about class barriers?

'Margaret Thatcher's movie makes the world of the House of Commons in London look too beautiful, but it has a high cost.' Discuss using formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ Do you like movies with beautiful pictures or movies with great dialogue?

'Margaret Thatcher is not a nice person because they only care about cognitive decay.' Give your opinion using formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ Do you like the ending of the movie 'The Iron Lady', or do you want a different ending?

'Margaret Thatcher's movie 'The Iron Lady' is too simple and does not show deep feelings about paranoia.' Talk about this with formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ Did your ideas about paranoia change after watching this movie?

'Margaret Thatcher's problem of confronting class barriers, parliamentary debates, and late-life cognitive decline never ends because they cannot agree on guilt-stricken.' Explain using formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ What was the most beautiful scene in the movie?

'The screenplay of 'The Iron Lady' would have achieved a far more profound existential resonance had the director opted for a non-linear structure.' Speculate using formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ Under what circumstances would you consider translating your personal experiences into a dramatic screenplay?

'The supporting cast, specifically her husband Denis Thatcher, parliamentary ministers, and critics, serve as the true ideological engine of 'The Iron Lady', overshadowing Margaret Thatcher.' Evaluate using formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ Which aspect of cinematic craftsmanship (sound design, color grading, editing tempo) has the most visceral impact on your emotions?

'The precise framing and meticulous sound design (or use of silence) in the House of Commons in London visually represent absolute entrapment.' Deconstruct with formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ If you were executive producing a contemporary reimagining of 'The Iron Lady', what structural modifications would you introduce?

'The recursive visual motifs throughout 'The Iron Lady' function as a sophisticated subtextual dialogue with the viewer.' Discuss using formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ If you were granted an audience with the director of 'The Iron Lady', what specific stylistic choice would you ask them to defend?

'The film's ultimate worldview is one of uncompromising nihilism, offering no avenues of redemption.' Debate this using formal Subjunctive & Parliamentary Command.
★ If you were to archive a single frame from 'The Iron Lady' as a representative artifact of modern visual culture, which would you select?

ul.li: Incorrect: I recommend you to see this film → Correct: I recommend that you see this film (Use 'recommend that + subjunctive/bare infinitive' or 'recommend doing'.)
Incorrect: The reason is because she was afraid → Correct: The reason is that she was afraid (Avoid 'the reason is because'; use 'the reason is that' for formal/style clarity.)
Incorrect: Seldom I have seen such an ending → Correct: Seldom have I seen such an ending (Negative adverbs like 'seldom' at the beginning of a clause trigger subject-auxiliary inversion.)
